1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.
None has appeared for respondent no.2 despite notice.

2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.73 of 2024, under Section 364, 354, 323, 504,
506, 376(3) IPC, Section 5/6 & 7/8 of PCOSO Act, Section 3(2)5, 3(1)Da, Dha of SC/ST Act &
Section 3/25 of Arms Act, P.S. Harchandpur, District Rae Bareli.

sentences.text: In terms of the FIR lodged on 22.02.2024 it was alleged that the victim aged about 15 years was coming from college when the accused named in the FIR came on a four wheeler and pulled the victim in their car after showing a country-made pistol.
It was also stated that she was misbehaved and were beaten very badly and caste related abuses were hurled.

4. In the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim stated that she knew the applicant since Class 10th and used to talk on telephone allegedly under the threats of killing the father of the victim.
It was also stated that the applicant used to visit her home frequently and physical relations were also formed and a video was also made.

It was also stated that the applicant used to blackmail her and in January, 2024, an amount of Rs.95,000/- was drawn after making forged signatures in the cheque book of the grandfather of the victim.
She also stated that these facts were revealed to her family members who asked her not to talk to him and ultimately, on 22.02.2024, the victim was pulled in a car with all the four persons.
It was also stated that they were misbehaving with her and touching her inappropriately.
5. In the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the victim reiterated the said version with regard to the incident that had allegedly took place on 22.02.2024.

She, however, stated that when she opened both the doors of the car, the car met with the accident and the public caught hold of them; no allegations of offence under Section 376 IPC were levelled in the said statement.

6. Learned AGA opposes the bail application and points out towards the recovery wherein the police authorities saw that vehicle being Maruti 800 was standing near the road and the accused were running, however, the victim was sitting in the car.
The said recovery is contradictory to the allegations levelled in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., where it was stated that it was the public which caught hold the accused.

7. Considering the statements including the statement of the victim that the applicant and the victim knew each other and physical relations were also formed in between then, a case for bail is made out, particularly, when the applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 23.02.2024.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant Aman Singh be released on bail in aforesaid FIR number on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
